ts11_churches.topic: Catholic, Orthodox and mainline Protestant positions on Christian Zionism and Israel/Palestine

claims.text: Herzl's diary records Pius X's answer in January 1904: 'Non possumus'; 'The Jews have not recognized our Lord, therefore we cannot recognize the Jewish people'; if Jews settled in Palestine 'we shall have churches and priests ready to baptize all of you'. Audience arranged by Count Berthold Dominik Lippay. (CCJR dates the diary entry 26 January 1904; Encyclopaedia Judaica gives the audience as 25 January.)

Catechism of the Catholic Church 676: the Antichrist's deception 'already begins to take shape in the world' whenever the claim is made to realise within history the messianic hope; the Church has rejected even modified forms of millenarianism, especially the political form of secular messianism.

Nostra Aetate 4 (1965): 'God holds the Jews most dear for the sake of their Fathers'; the Passion 'cannot be charged against all the Jews, without distinction, then alive' nor against Jews today; Jews 'should not be presented as rejected or accursed by God'; decries 'displays of anti-Semitism, directed against Jews at any time and by anyone'. The text says nothing about the land or a state.

Holy See–State of Palestine Comprehensive Agreement signed 26 June 2015, in force 2 January 2016; Basic Agreement with the PLO 15 February 2000; Israeli Foreign Ministry called it one-sided, saying recognition 'damages the peace process by strengthening Palestinian refusal to negotiate'.

Patriarchs and Heads of Churches of the Holy Land, statement dated 17 January 2026 (published 18 January): Christian Zionism among 'damaging ideologies' that 'mislead the public, sow confusion, and harm the unity of our flock'; objected its promoters were 'welcomed at official levels both locally and internationally'; followed a Washington Post report of about 1,000 evangelical pastors visiting Israel in early January and Netanyahu calling evangelicals Israel's 'closest allies' on 31 December 2025.

Huckabee replied that no 'sect of the Christian faith should claim exclusivity in speaking for Christians worldwide' and that 'Christian Zionism' is used 'in a pejorative manner to disparage free-church believers' (X, 20 January 2026).
OSV quotes the 2006 Jerusalem Declaration: Christian Zionism 'detrimental to a just peace within Palestine and Israel'; 'We categorically reject Christian Zionist doctrines as false teaching.'

Theologians answering the 2026 statement (MEF, 20 Jan 2026): André Villeneuve (Sacred Heart Major Seminary) says Zionism 'is not the product of nineteenth-century Protestant dispensationalism'; Gavin D'Costa on 'Catholic Zionism'; Gerald McDermott; A.J. Nolte (Regent University).

PC(USA) General Assembly voted 310–303 on 20 June 2014 to divest from Caterpillar, Hewlett-Packard and Motorola Solutions (holdings about $21m); a 2012 proposal failed by two votes; measure reaffirmed Israel's right to exist; supporters said it was not part of BDS; Israeli Embassy called it 'shameful'; AJC said 'driven by hatred of Israel'; Rabbi Rick Jacobs said PC(USA) no longer 'a partner' on peace work.

January 2016: Wespath (UMC General Board of Pension and Health Benefits, >$20bn) excluded five Israeli banks (Hapoalim, Leumi, First International, Israel Discount, Mizrahi Tefahot), citing 'high-risk' countries.

UMC General Conference (Charlotte, 23 April–3 May 2024) approved on a consent calendar on 30 April 2024 a resolution asking UM institutions not to buy government bonds of Israel, Turkey and Morocco over long-term occupations; advisory, does not bind Wespath; Wespath held about 0.12% of investments in the three countries' sovereign debt at end-2023; written by United Methodists for Kairos Response (Lisa Bender).

ts11_palestinian.topic: Palestinian Christians and their theological answer to Christian Zionism

claims.text: Kairos Palestine launched in Bethlehem 11 December 2009; panel chaired by former Latin Patriarch Michel Sabbah; authors include Sabbah, Archbishop Atallah Hanna, Bishop Munib Younan (later asked removal per Lowe), coordinator Rifat Kassis.

Kairos text: occupation 'a sin against God and humanity'; 'any theology that legitimizes the occupation is far from Christian teachings'; calls churches 'to revisit theologies that justify crimes perpetrated against our people and the dispossession of the land'; 'non-violent resistance to this injustice is a right and duty'; calls for divestment and boycott 'of everything produced by the occupation'. The term 'heresy' was not found in the excerpts checked.

Lowe's critique: section 4.3 says 'the roots of "terrorism" are in the human injustice committed and in the evil of the occupation'; he reads the scare quotes and 'resistance' as euphemistic; no outright rejection of terrorism in the excerpts.

Naim Ateek, born Beisan 1937, family displaced to Nazareth 1948; Anglican priest 1967, canon of St George's, Jerusalem; Justice, and Only Justice (1989) first articulation of Palestinian liberation theology; founded Sabeel (1991 or 1994, dates differ); Sabeel endorsed Kairos 2009; 2001 Easter message 'one huge golgotha'.

Christ at the Checkpoint: biennial conference of Bethlehem Bible College, first held 2010; objective to 'create a platform for serious engagement with Christian Zionism'; 2012 manifesto: 'Any exclusive claim to land of the Bible in the name of God is not in line with the teaching of Scripture'; speakers included Joel Hunter (2012), Geoff Tunnicliffe of WEA (2014).
CUFI's David Brog said the message is 'resonating' and 'This generation is in play' (2014).

ICEJ (4 Mar 2012): conference gives 'a one-sided message based on a deeply flawed historical narrative'; warns of 'Cloaked versions of Replacement theology'; some speakers went 'into outright anti-Semitism'.

Munther Isaac: Lutheran pastor in Bethlehem (ordained 2016), CATC director from 2012; books From Land to Lands (2015), The Other Side of the Wall (2020), Christ in the Rubble (2025); Christmas Eve 2023 'Christ in the Rubble' liturgy with nativity in rubble; Bethlehem–Jerusalem permit cancelled; reviewers say he disregards Israeli security concerns.
Palestinian Christians: about 12% of the population early in the 20th century; about 47,000–50,000 in the West Bank and East Jerusalem (~1%, 2017 census); about 1,000 in Gaza before the war.

St Porphyrius compound strike 19 Oct 2023: 18 civilians killed; Israeli military said it hit a Hamas 'command and control centre'; Amnesty (20 Nov 2023) found no sign of a military objective and called it reckless, amounting to a war crime.

Holy Family Church, Gaza City, 17 July 2025: three killed, about ten injured including Fr Gabriel Romanelli; Israeli Foreign Ministry: 'Israel never targets churches'; Netanyahu regretted 'stray ammunition'; Pizzaballa: 'they hit the church directly'; Vatican called the attack 'unjustifiable'.
July 2025 arson at St George's church, Taybeh, West Bank.

ts11_generations.topic: Evangelical dissent and the generational shift in polls

claims.text: Gary Burge: about 25 years at Wheaton College, Calvin Theological Seminary 2017–2023, PC(USA) minister; Whose Land? Whose Promise? (2003; rev. 2013); Jesus and the Land (2010).

Inbari and Bumin (book Christian Zionism in the Twenty-First Century; TAU release 12 Feb 2024): among evangelicals under 30, support for Israel 68.9% (2018) to 33.6% (2021); for Palestinians 'a little over 5%' to 24.3%; neither 25% to 42.2%; almost seven in ten young evangelicals post- or amillennial (spring 2021); premillennial pastors older; Inbari: social media, 'a sort of youthful rebellion', 'a perfect storm'. Sample sizes not stated.

Pew, fieldwork 4–17 May 2026, 12,574 adults, ±1.3: white evangelical Protestants 'the only religious group in which a majority (57%) have a favorable view of the Israeli government'; 74% favourable to Israeli people, 33% Palestinian people. Catholics 34% favourable to Israeli government; white non-evangelical Protestants 33%; Black Protestants 30%; Jews 47%. All adults: 32% (47% in 2022).

Pew 2026 by age, favourable to Israeli government: total 18% (18–29), 25%, 40%, 47% (65+); Republicans 28%, 38%, 61%, 75%; Democrats 12%, 15%, 19%, 21%. Israeli people, Republicans: 42%, 55%, 75%, 83%. Republicans overall favourable to Israeli government 65% (2022) to 51% (2026).
Per Crosswalk's report of Pew, white evangelicals favourable to Israeli government fell from 71% (2024) to 57% (2026), to Israeli people from 84% to 74%.
